answers.quote: Part XVIII of the Constitution speaks of emergency provisions. The emergency provisions therein can be classified into three categories: (a) Articles 352, 353, 354, 358 and 359 which relate to emergency proper - if we can use that expression, (b) Articles 355, 356 and 357 which deal with imposition of President's rule in States in a certain situation and (c) Article 360 which speaks of financial emergency.
answers.notes: c46 classifies Part XVIII as emergency provisions (352/353/354/358/359, 355/356/357, 360).

answers.notes: c01: the President may proclaim an Emergency under Art 352(1).

answers.quote: If the President is satisfied that a grave emergency exists whereby the security of India or of any part of the territory thereof is threatened, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion, he may, by Proclamation, make a declaration to that effect in respect of the whole of India or of such part of the territory thereof as may be specified in the Proclamation.

answers.notes: c34 says the rectification made written Union Cabinet advice necessary together with the 'armed rebellion' ground; c14 attributes the armed-rebellion substitution to the 44th Amendment Act 1978 and c49 refers to Art 352 as amended by the 44th Amendment — the written-advice requirement itself is not named to the 44th in a single claim, hence LIKELY.
